svg.title: Escape Room Adventure | Swing and application boundaries

g.text: Escape Room Adventure | Swing and application boundaries
All seven pairs appear in escape-room-use-cases.puml.
The domain checks the complete inventory.
move() schedules moveRoom.execute(), with no destination input.
Gate rules and automatic item transfers belong to Game.
For ItemLock, requiredItems lists ALL exact IDs and labels.
Game.itemDetails resolves labels across rooms + inventory;
the assembler uses read-only metadata, never a snapshot.
heldRequiredIds = required IDs intersect actual inventory.
canUnlock = ACTIVE + accessible locked door + containsAll.
TriviaData(lockId, prompt, choices); no expected answer
LockData describes the current Room's doorLock and exitChallenge.
Menu/no-game output sets canMove=false and finalRoom=false.
The UI receives no successor ID or destination list.
message displays action/result text plus only newly obtained item names.
There is no available-item list or separate obtain command.
Show required item names and which are held.
Rebuild options after every result; send stable object/item/lock IDs.
one movement button, save/load. Answers use the answer field.
The movement button reads Next room or Escape from finalRoom,
is enabled by canMove, and calls controller.move().
One serial worker runs all game commands and HTTP/file work.
SwingUiDispatcher posts model updates to the EDT.
dispatch sets busy/guard before scheduling. finally posts an EDT
completion callback AFTER the queued presenter output/render.
That callback clears ViewModel busy and the atomic guard together;
new commands remain rejected until the result has rendered.
Presenter builds GameViewState INSIDE its EDT callback, preserving
the model's CURRENT busy; worker-side busy is never captured.
No Swing/executor types enter use_case or entity.
Every command outcome produces fresh immutable output,
including errors and changed=false, then presenter -> EDT
model -> View render. Reads and rendering never acquire items.
fromGame(game, message, activeLockId) keeps three arguments.
Wrong answers retain the same active question; an uninitialized
submit or API failure uses no active question.
Load/refresh never repeat an Obtained notice for held items.
Dark blue = view / app: GameView, AppBuilder, SwingCommandDispatcher, SwingUiDispatcher.
Light blue = interface_adapter: GameController, GamePresenter, GameViewModel, GameViewState, CommandDispatcher, UiDispatcher.
Green = use_case; yellow = entity (full state in domain diagram); purple = data_access.
Repeated classes are focused views of the same types; constructors initialize all stored collaborators.
AppBuilder.build() injects the graph with local variables. GameView receives immutable UI data only.
Action.appearingItemIds names existing own-room items; Game preflights ALL acquisitions before applying effects.
Game automatically transfers new appearing items to inventory; already-held IDs are skipped without another notice.
New-game/first-entry visible items are acquired atomically before output; restore never replays room entry.
Effects change room object state only; inventory display and message are the existing acquisition output.
UseItem validates exact required IDs in the complete inventory; items remain held after success.
Trivia.open fetches and installs an API question once; submit reuses it. Errors permit retry.
Door ItemLock and room exit Trivia can complete in either order; actions do not unlock either gate.
Game.canMove() = ACTIVE AND Room.canLeave(); canLeave requires BOTH gates on the validated single path.
Game.move() preflights Room.nextRoomId before mutation: present -> next room; empty -> ESCAPED.
The immutable template defines one finite path covering every configured room once, with no revisits.
Game returns DomainResult(code, changed, resultText); interactors assemble fresh output.
